timeline.message:
Handle scheduler shutdown in `MasterService`

Today if `ThreadPool#scheduler` is shut down while submitting a task for
execution by the `MasterService` then we directly throw the rejection
exception to the caller. By the looks of it most callers don't expect
this method to throw anything, so this commit adjusts the behaviour to
fail the task instead.

Closes #105549
timeline.author: David Turner

Today if `ThreadPool#scheduler` is shut down while submitting a task for

exception to the caller. By the looks of it most callers don't expect
this method to throw anything, so this commit adjusts the behaviour to
fail the task instead.

Closes #105549
Should it be more specific and only catch rejection?

reply.body: I think it can only be a rejection, but there's no good reason to let anything else escape here. I added an assertion in 01e4c816cf3.

reply.body: Sorry should have said - the stack trace in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/105549 is kinda useless because it uses `actionGet()` which strips off the outer `ExecutionException` so you can't see who is treating this exception as a test failure.

timeline.body: Not in this patch, but should we have something like `String AbstractRunnable#identifyTask()` that returns unique(-ish) identifiers for a `Runnable`, so we don't have to do things like `toString` matching?

reply.body: That's kinda what `toString()` is for. It's just that the automatically generated unique identifier is kinda useless.
I was thinking something that didn't involve string parsing -- toString seems geared towards log messages, not equality checks.

I know what you mean, I would do something more robust if this were production code for sure. On balance I think this is best for testing purposes tho - the alternative adds a little too much stuff to production just to support this test.

timeline.body: "Only count errors that exactly match the failure we inject above. Any others are unexpected."

reply.body: Is that a note-to-self or a suggested comment? :)

timeline.body:
So this is setting up the DeterministicTaskQueue's ThreadPool to execute this code before any Runnable? Could we have a comment about what this is doing? Maybe something like,

"The MasterService wraps update tasks in TaskTimeoutHandlers. Set up the thread pool to check for TaskTimeoutHandler Runnables, and artificially inject an error, but otherwise allow anything else to run as normal."

reply.body:
I think name dropping MasterService and TaskTimeoutHandler class names might make it easier to go find the code -- I had to grep using the expected `r.toString()` value below. 

But the comment gives a hint, so I'm content and will leave it up to you.
How about this: I extracted the method that generates the string to `org.elasticsearch.cluster.service.MasterService#getTimeoutTaskDescription`, that way you can use `Find usages` to join the dots.
Actually we can just inline this, this was more useful in the test from which I copied it. Simplest to just have the implementation right there rather than indirect via a name
A good name can be very informative :) But that works, too 👍
